articleTitle: Studying the Knowledge and Behavior of ChatGPT via Journey to the West
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: Recent research showed that large language models (LLMs) can generate high-quality content capable of performing various NLP tasks and exhibiting remarkable performance. However, these LLMs are also known for their ridiculously wrong contents, also known as hallucinations, that significantly decrease their correctness in safety-sensitive applications. This paper aims to study the correctness of state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs like GPTs by investigating their behavior using simple questions. The author selects one of the most famous Chinese novels to build the question-answer pairs and study how SOTA LLMs behave against misleading information and rethinking strategies. The results indicate that both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 are prone to be misled by simply denying their correct answers. They can also improve their correctness by rethinking and answering again without any external knowledge.

articleTitle: Credibility Evaluation of Aircraft HWIL Simulation Based on the Time-Varying Area Metric
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: Credibility evaluation of aircraft HWIL simulation is usually measured by the degree of consistency between simulation test data and the measured data. A new method for evaluating the credibility of aircraft HWIL simulation is established based on the idea of time-varying area measurement and uncertainty measurement Mainly for univariate, single simulation, multivariable and multi-simulation. The DTW distance measurement method is used to obtain the weight coefficients of correlated multiple response variables, and the effectiveness of uncertainty measurement method in obtaining the credibility of aircraft HWIL simulation at a certain level of confidence is verified through typical examples.

articleTitle: Assessing Programming Proficiency Through Eye Gaze Analysis Using Fine-Tuned Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: The exploration of human eye movement data offers a groundbreaking approach to assessing programming expertise, marking a significant stride in advancing STEM education. This research explores the capabilities of fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to assess the programming proficiency of readers by analyzing their eye movements during the reading of program code. To achieve this, we fine-tuned the LLMs using the largest eye movement in programming dataset that is publicly available. Subsequently, we executed a series of experiments to evaluate the efficacy of our fine-tuned models in assessing programming skills based on eye movement traces.

articleTitle: Automated Classification and Grading of Power System Database Fields Based on Rule Association and Probabilistic Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: Recent advancements in power system databases have led to a significant increase in the amount of data field entries, which in turn requires efficient classification and grading methods. This paper proposes an automated approach to classify and grade power system database fields using rule association and probabilistic reasoning. The purpose of this study is to develop a reliable method to accurately classify and grade the various fields in power system databases. The research methodology involves creating a set of rules based on association analysis and using probabilistic reasoning to determine the field grades. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves high classification accuracy and grading consistency. The study concludes that the automated method can effectively classify and grade power system database fields, thereby facilitating efficient data analysis and decision-making processes.

articleTitle: An Architecture for Industrial Control Mimic Systems Based on Component and Multi-Level 2-Mode Judgment Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: As industrial control systems become more prevalent, cybersecurity concerns have gained significant attention. Mimic defense technology, serving as an effective security measure, combats network threats by continuously switching between functionally identical entities. However, current mimic control systems still have various shortcomings in executor design and judgment techniques, such as fixed heterogeneous executors and inefficient arbitration processes. In response to these challenges, this study introduces a component-based architecture for mimic control systems, enabling dynamic executor generation through modularized communication while minimizing system invasiveness. Additionally, a multi-level 2-mode judgment algorithm is designed, consider both real-time performance and security requirements, dynamically balancing decision efficiency and result reliability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach not only enhances the decision efficiency of mimic industrial control systems but also improves the judgment efficiency of mimic systems.

articleTitle: RCW-Pruner: Row-Column Wise Pruning Framework on Systolic Array
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: To accelerate CNN models on edge devices, the coordination of model pruning and the systolic array is an efficient paradigm. However, because of the mismatch of the irregular sparsity of the pruned model and the dedicated regular architecture of the systolic array, the pruned model is hard to cash the theoretical acceleration. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes the RCW-Pruner which prunes the weights by the granularity of systolic array's row and column. Without any hardware modification, the pruned network can bring significant benefits of performance improvement by skipping the computing of those rows and columns. The experimental results exhibit that the RCW-Pruner achieves an average speedup of 2.62 times, 3.4 times and 2.36 times on 32 × 32, 64 × 64 and 128 × 128 systolic arrav, respectively,

articleTitle: Research on Test Data Expansion Method Based on UAV Typical Index Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: In order to scientifically and effectively evaluate the performance indexes of aircraft, the common Bayes multi-source data fusion method can comprehensively utilize a variety of information types under the condition that the decision risk is as small as possible, but there are risks such as insufficient data utilization and small sample data being “submerged” by large sample data in the fusion. This paper proposes a test data expansion method based on the combination of probability features and BP neural network model, and is verified by typical application to ensure that the sample size of multi-source data is comparable. Supplementary data not only retains the probability features of the original data, but also the sample generation has physical connotation.

articleTitle: Optimized Gauss-Hermite Quadrature: A Refined Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: For nonlinear problems involving Gaussian inte-grals, the Gauss-Hermite quadrature is preferred. The optimized Gauss-Hermite quadrature can outperform the conventional Gauss-Hermite quadrature through the optimal quadrature points and weights. However, obtaining the optimal quadrature points and weights presents challenges, mainly due to the complexity of constrained nonlinear least-squares fitting in an adaptive sampling. This paper introduces a novel approach to optimizing the Gauss-Hermite quadrature, distinguishing itself from prior works by addressing the optimization as an uncon-strained nonlinear least-squares problem. This modification not only simplifies the optimization problem but also enables the derivation of an exact gradient formula, significantly improving the employment of gradient-based optimization algorithms. Furthermore, we develop a deterministic grid strategy to bolster the method's efficacy. The superiority of the new approach is demonstrated via two numerical examples, showing its accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Industrial 5G Service Allocation Based on A Novel Bidirectional Selection Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: This paper proposes a server-client mutual selection strategy based on multiple resource indicators, providing a balanced selection algorithm for edge compu-ting services for industrial Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs). Firstly, based on the service popularity and Zipf's law, the type of service primarily carried by each Remote Unit (RU) is determined, and RUs are divided into work area slices based on the similarity of service popularity. Nest, the AGV side first sends a forward service request to the RU side based on the requirements and urgency of work tasks, and then the RU side reversely selects the AGV from the perspective of optimal resource allocation. This paper comprehensively considers multiple factors such as matching of process service content, user de-lay limit, and computing and communication resources, and can solve the problem of dynamically allocating resources in the edge-cloud computing network in a balanced matching manner in scenarios like intelligent factories and ports. Simultaneously, this paper adopts the strategy of bidirectional selection, achieving a trade-off between user experience and economic benefits for users and operators.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator on FPGA for Crystallography Spot Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: The X-rays from a light source produce a lot of data in a very short period of time, and only a tiny fraction of it is meaningful to study. Traditional statistics-based methods rely heavily on experienced experts to classify it. How to obtain these data efficiently and accurately is one of the challenges that light sources are now facing. To solve this problem, a new FPGA-based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) accelerator is introduced for screening Bragg spots in diffraction images produced at electron laser light sources. The proposed method enhances the target by filtering the data and aims at the region of interest through heat map analysis. A lightweight hardware-friendly convolutional neural network architecture called BraggNet is proposed. The proposed network contains a feature extractor and a classifier. Quantization and layer fusion method is proposed to compression the model. The accelerator uses pipelining between layers and on-chip quantized weight reuse to reduce the time of data transfer process. Data streaming is used between layers in the accelerator. The proposed accelerator is implemented using HLS and FPGA ZCU104. The results show that the proposed method achieves 82.66% accuracy of BraggNet, and 82.16% accuracy of quantized BraggNet, which is higher than the existing method. The proposed method is suitable for data screening at the receiving end of the light source detector.

articleTitle: BTPA: Hardware-Software Co-Design for Bitwise Based Transformer with Parallelized Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: In recent years, the Transformer algorithm has achieved outstanding results in many areas. However, the Transformer algorithm relies on the self-attention mechanism, which requires a large amount of computation with quadratic complexity and large memory resources, hindering its popularity in edge devices. Most existing studies focus on reducing the algorithm complexity by selecting part of the elements instead of all elements to participate the calculation of the attention, but do not explicitly consider the efficiency of deploying their methods on edge devices which is suffering from the float point matrix multiplication. This paper proposes a software-hardware collaborative self-attention module, which adopts bitwise operations to replace the traditional float point matrix multiplication while retaining the ability of the attention mechanism to capture complex long-range information dependencies with the reduction of algorithm complexity and memory consumption. Meanwhile, we design a dedicated acceleration operator on Xilinx ZCU104 FPGA. The experimental results show that the proposed operator achieves a speedup of more than 1300× compared with the traditional self-attention operator with only 0.8% performance loss in CIFAR image classification task.

articleTitle: TurboFed: A Federated Learning Approach to The PHM of Distributed Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: This paper proposes one approach with federated learning technique to address practical challenges faced by the emerging green energy industries, i.e., wind turbines in terms of Predictive Health Management (PHM). Not as many federated learning applications being used in the scenarios only for simulation, the application of federated learning in this paper is focused on the real industrial problems with raw data collected from the fields. Huge amount of real data was collected by sensors on more than ten wind turbines across different areas in China and transmitted to the storage for in-time processing. The framework proposed in this paper called TurboFed, can handle the raw data and achieves good prediction performance in the practical wind generated power systems. The framework showed its help on improving the efficiency of the wind turbines. The paper has brought three novel results. First, as far as known, the framework here is the first federated learning framework addressing position adjustment of wind turbines in the real environment. Second, it deploys customized recurrent neural computing models to the wind turbines which are considered the client devices under the federated learning paradigm. Finally, it incorporates new customized aggregation algorithms on the sever side.

articleTitle: Maximizing the Total Utility of Requesters in Crowdsourcing
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: Crowdsourcing coordinates a large group of workers online to do small tasks published by requesters on a crowd-sourcing platform. In the literature, the model used by many papers assumes that one task is given to and completed by one worker only. In this paper, we consider a model that extends this model in space and time. Based on our model, we formulate an optimization problem from the perspective of the requesters that maximizes the utility of all the requesters subject to the constraint that the total workload given to a worker should not exceed his capability. We then provide a solution to the problem and design distributed algorithms for the requesters and the workers to interact with each other in multiple rounds. After that, we give a concrete example to explain the solution and the algorithms. Then, we discuss the convergence speed of our algorithms using different methods. Finally, we conduct simulations to compare these convergence methods and draw conclusions.

articleTitle: HPC-Crash: Characterizing Crash-Proneness of HPC Programs from Various Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: High-Performance Computing (HPC) systems are widely used to execute large-scale, complex applications. How-ever, with the integration of more cores, HPC systems become more susceptible to soft errors, which can incur crash cases in HPC systems. Typically, the Checkpoint and Recovery (CR) mechanism is the standard solution to recover from crashes while it will incur significant overhead. Although many works have been proposed to minimize the overhead of CR mechanisms, we observe they may ignore the application's inherent error resilience features, thereby missing some opportunities for further CR mechanism optimization. Therefore, this paper proposes HPC-Crash, a framework that can fine-grained characterize the Crash characteristics of the HPC benchmark from various perspectives. By leveraging HPC-Crash to perform exhaustive statistics analysis for 5 HPC benchmarks, we observe instruction type, execution region, and application workflow are all essential factors for crash-proneness in HPC programs. The characterizing results of HPC-Crash will provide essential insight for HPC programmers to design more cost-effective CR solutions.

articleTitle: Design of Anti-Interference Path Planning for Cellular-Connected UAVs Based on Improved DDPG
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: The flight and communication security of the Cellular-Connected Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is an important and popular research direction. Due to the complexity of the environmental space, UAVs face a complex and ever-changing task space. In recent years, reinforcement learning has rapidly advanced and widely applied in complex scenarios path planning problems. However, due to the discrete action space, their accuracy is limited. To address aforementioned problems, a new method for UAV path planning based on Deep Reinforcement Learning has been proposed in this paper. Specifically, this paper adopts an improved DDPG method with Actor-Critic framework, which can improve the accuracy. To further enhance the algorithm's precision and training speed, this paper introduces Post-Decision State method, which leverages experience for prediction to optimize the training results and enable UAVs to adapt to the ever-changing environment. Simulation experiments have proved that the improved method can increase training speed and make significant improvements in path performance.

articleTitle: Index Multilinear Tree-based Cross Chain for Decentralized Identity Governance
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: Decentralized identity has become an integral part of digital development. However, while ensuring privacy protection in distributed digital identity, achieving limited cost storage and retrieval of identity information remains a complex issue. Distributed storage often comes with significant costs and hinders rapid data retrieval. In this paper, we propose the use of index multilinear trees for data storage to enable fast identity information retrieval. Furthermore, based on the sidechain method in blockchain cross-chain technology, we propose storing the root hash of the index multilinear tree on the sidechain, offering a low-cost interoperability solution for complete information stored on the sidechain. We analyze the cost of this solution and conduct experimental performance testing to demonstrate its efficiency.

articleTitle: MEC Multi-Objective Task Offloading Algorithm for Joint Energy and Latency Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: This paper focuses on developing a multi-objective optimization algorithm designed for task offloading within the context of mobile edge computing (MEC). The primary objective is to investigate and enhance the performance of MEC systems concerning task offloading. The initial step involves constructing a MEC multi-objective task offloading scenario. Subsequently, a comprehensive presentation of the system model within this scenario is provided. The paper introduces a MEC task offloading scheduling strategy based on multi-objective optimization. This strategy is developed in conjunction with an analysis of the computational offloading process, with a specific emphasis on optimizing both the optimal delay and energy consumption associated with computational offloading.

articleTitle: An Integrated Method for Electric Power Data Cleaning and Anomaly Detection Based on Multidimensional Semantic Similarity and Deep Auto-Encoding
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated method for electric power data cleaning and anomaly detection based on multidimensional semantic similarity and deep auto-encoding. The background of the study is the increasing complexity and size of electric power data, which pose challenges for data cleaning and anomaly detection. The purpose of this study is to develop an effective method to address these challenges. The method consists of two main steps: multidimensional semantic similarity calculation and deep auto-encoding-based anomaly detection. Firstly, multidimensional semantic similarity is calculated to measure the similarity between different data points and detect potential anomalies. Then, deep auto-encoding is applied to learn the high-level representations of the power data and detect anomalies based on the reconstruction error. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in data cleaning and anomaly detection for electric power data. In conclusion, the integrated method based on multidimensional semantic similarity and deep auto-encoding is effective in electric power data cleaning and anomaly detection, providing a useful tool for im-proving the reliability and quality of power grid operations.

articleTitle: Understanding Nutrient Loads Delivered From Mississippi-Atchafalaya River Basin to Gulf of Mexico Using Tree-Based Regression Model
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: The objective of this study is to identify and develop predictive models of nutrient loads collected from United States Geological Survey (USGS) monitored stations in the Mississippi-Atchafalaya River Basin to (MARB) and to better understand the nature of excess nutrient loads delivered from the MARB to the Gulf of Mexico. Random Forest Regression (RFR) and Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR) are used to capture the temporal structure of nutrient load changes. The results will be used in further studies to estimate and predict nutrient concentrations and fluxes into the Gulf of Mexico. In future, innovative remote sensing techniques could be employed to gather information about nutrient loads, and engineers may contribute to the design and implementation of more intelligent systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Distribution Network Asset Effectiveness and Investment Decision-Making: A Study Based on the Multidimensional Lean Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: In recent years, lean management has emerged as a significant trend across diverse industries, notably in the power sector. This study focuses on evaluating and enhancing the effectiveness of distribution network assets within the evolving power industry. Aligned with the strategic goals of the State Grid Corporation, it emphasizes optimizing investment, costs, and depreciation while reducing inefficient expenditures. A multidimensional lean management system is proposed, facilitating the integration of finance and operations. This system enables a transition from financial language to business language and provides reliable data support for tariff determination, budget allocation, and business management. The research emphasizes improving the service capabilities of accounting information by adapting to the evolving business environment. It promotes a managerial transformation of traditional accounting information systems, supporting precise incentives and performance evaluations. Furthermore, the study highlights the significance of enhancing the level of information technology within the State Grid Corporation. Advanced big data analysis methods enable the extraction of valuable insights for asset analysis and investment decision-making, promoting digitization and management modernization. Overall, this research contributes to the transformation and modernization of the power grid industry, enabling informed decision-making and improved management performance.

articleTitle: Novel Metric to Predict NBA Regular Season MVP
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: The pursuit of the Most Valuable Player (MVP) award has always been a goal for all National Basketball Association (NBA) players. Becoming MVP can be considered the ultimate recognition of their individual worth. However, aside from the past MVPs, the NBA has seen many great stars emerge over the past 75 years, all of whom have displayed remarkable skill and talent. In this fast-paced era of digital connectivity, not everyone can watch an entire game to judge a player's abilities comprehensively. People often rely on basic statistics such as shooting percentage or rebound percentage to make an initial assessment of a player. The MVP award is typically determined through a voting process by professional independent media personnel after the conclusion of the regular season. Many individuals seek to predict the final MVP results by analyzing players' basic statistics from the regular season. We believe that a player's value should not solely be determined by basic statistics. An MVP should be someone who can elevate the performance of their teammates and contribute significantly on both ends of the court. As a result, this article introduces a new evaluation metric for MVP prediction, which aims to assess a player's positive and negative impact on their teammates. This metric is proposed to gauge a superstar's true value to the team, and it is used in conjunction with advanced statistics to predict the players most likely to be named MVP.

articleTitle: A System for Data Fusion of Multi-Source Wireless Monitoring Devices and Identification of Illegal FM Broadcast Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: In response to the escalating development of wireless monitoring devices and system platforms by radio regulatory authorities across the nation, the imperative for an efficient and secure data fusion platform has emerged. This platform facilitates the integration and sharing of diverse information from domestic and international wireless monitoring devices, fostering cross-domain and cross-system collaboration. It not only standardizes data and protocols but also optimizes resource utilization, enhances efficiency, and ensures data security and privacy. Simultaneously, the routine monitoring of frequency modulation broadcast spectrum and the crackdown on illegal activities, such as unauthorized “pirate radio” stations, have become integral components of radio regulatory work. Addressing the challenges of current data fusion platforms, including differences in standards, data security, and data diversity, we propose a comprehensive system for wireless monitoring devices. Leveraging innovative atomization concepts and the efficient JavaSSM framework, our system modularizes data processing and service validation tasks, ensuring reliability and stability in practical operations. Additionally, we introduce a method for monitoring frequency modulation broadcast signals, utilizing template-based comparisons and speech-to-text keyword matching algorithms. This approach aims to identify illegal signals, including “pirate radio”, by evaluating spectrum thresholds and conducting comparisons with a secure signal library. The system further employs speech-to-text operations and keyword matching for the detection of illicit broadcast content. Our research contributes to the evolving field of wireless monitoring, providing a robust solution for the identification and prevention of unauthorized broadcasts.

articleTitle: High-Performance Virtual Reality Services via Multi-network Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 10th IEEE International Conference on High Performance and Smart Computing (HPSC)
abstract: Recent advancements in hardware technology and high-speed Gigabit WiFi solutions have paved the way for sig-nificant enhancements in Internet throughput, thereby enabling more sophisticated applications such as the combination of live streaming and virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) applications. Despite the growth, VR/ AR live broadcasting has a notably high computational demand for video stitching and encoding. Traditional methods rely on local resources, which are often insufficient. The advent of cloud computing offers a promising solution by outsourcing compute-intensive tasks to the cloud, thus alleviating the load on local systems. When uploading content to the cloud, a primary issue to address is how to ensure that footage captured from different cameras can arrive as synchronously as possible to effectively reduce processing latency. In this paper, we propose a novel mechanism that employs a multi-network interface controller at the acquisition terminals to enhance bandwidth utilization and ensure the synchronous arrival of multi-camera feeds for effective stitching. A multi-path transmission model is designed to manage potential network congestion and optimize buffer queue lengths in the cloud. Besides, a dynamic routing strategy is proposed to optimize the data forwarding by observing the instant network status. Our approach is validated through extensive simulations and prototype system experiments, demonstrating superior resource efficiency and performance over existing methods.
